digest.component_or_area: completion verifier banking and verdict assembly
propositions: At search exhaustion, BOUNDED_FALLBACK_EVIDENCE incorrectly banks met=false (refutation) when the actual state is insufficient evidence (absence-of-evidence misattributed as negative proof), producing false FAIL verdicts.

The banking write path and verdict assembly must distinguish three evidence outcomes (met, refuted, insufficient) via an optional framework-set evidence_sufficient:false marker alongside the bool met field, carried consistently through schema, validation, finalizer payload, and all rendering seams.

The marker must be written ONLY by the framework via a new CriterionBank.record_insufficient() call in the bounded fallback; model-facing tools remain bool-only; harvest_structured_into_bank preserves markers on markerless overwrites but lets bare met=false refutations replace them.

Both verdict consumers (close_precheck refusal and _render_verdict_text standalone renderer) must report insufficient evidence + remediation instead of unmet criteria when the top-level evidence_sufficient:false marker is present, while remaining fail-closed (FAIL verdict unchanged).

The audit/page.py completion-verdict consumer was discriminating PASS vs FAIL by payload shape (criteria presence); adding criteria[] to FAIL records for marker persistence broke that proxy, requiring the consumer to key on the verdict field instead.

The finalizer prompt and merge_finalizer_with_bank re-stamping must enforce that banked insufficient entries echo as met=false with insufficient-evidence findings, never bare refutation text; reconcile_verdict must derive the top-level marker (set iff FAIL, ≥1 unmet record carries per-criterion marker, and no unmet record lacks it).
